subtitle: Move an equity commitment from words to a clear proposed practice for your team, with appropriate responsibility, supporting evidence and planned follow-through.
scope: For leaders and staff across DHS who prepare team goals, work plans, position descriptions or priorities. This four-question drafting aid is optional preparation, not a definition of all equity work, an approval or the formal DHS analysis process. Actual hiring, accommodation, reporting, data use and other decisions retain their assigned authority and procedures. Use an example or private reflection rather than protected work records. For Native American- and Tribal-specific matters, contact the person or area responsible within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: A useful commitment can guide a team, and a clear practice can help carry it into work. This course uses a practice guidance project and hiring example to ask what would change, who has responsibility, what evidence fits and when review would help. Written plans support the work; they do not prove its effect. You can prepare a practice draft or examine your own assumptions privately. Actual decisions follow the processes that apply to them.

intro.heading: Connect a commitment to a proposed practice
intro.body:
A commitment can name what a team values and help explain why a proposed action matters. A written practice can make the action easier to coordinate. Neither should be dismissed because it takes another form. Equity work can exist in an established process, a separate plan, a daily decision or a relationship as well as a row in a work plan. Find what people actually do before concluding that a missing row means the work is absent.

Dana’s team is preparing guidance for partners. Its commitment is to make the guidance more usable. Dana proposes examining a sample with relevant willing users, recording questions and considering revisions before the planned release. This is a proposal, not evidence that the guidance is already accessible, that all users were represented or that the release improved an outcome.

Four optional drafting questions can clarify it: what task would change; who has responsibility and authority; what information could show what happened or helped; and when review would be useful. The answers depend on the issue. A review might examine usability observations and unresolved questions rather than a demographic count. An ongoing practice can use a release check or recurring discussion without becoming a one-time task.

The DHS Equity Policy establishes agency equity responsibilities and applicable analysis requirements. This course’s drafting questions do not replace them. For learning, use Dana’s an example or privately examine what a meaningful commitment looks like to you. A richer understanding can matter without a public story, edited work document or measured operational effect.

flashcards.back: A statement of purpose or value that can guide choices; it is not itself proof of an implemented change.
A specific way of working offered for consideration, with its purpose and remaining questions clear.
The person or role that carries a task within actual authority; consultation does not transfer every responsibility.
Information suited to the question and permitted to be used, with reliability, privacy and interpretation limits retained.
A suitable opportunity to examine progress or meaning; ongoing work can have useful recurring checks.
A proposed change, what was actually carried out, and what it contributed are separate claims.

items.title: Purpose and action belong together
items.body: Dana’s commitment explains why usability matters; the proposed sample review identifies a possible way to explore it. Keeping both can make the work understandable. A values statement is not an implemented result, but it need not be deleted or treated as worthless because it is not a task.

items.title: A draft is a bounded gain
items.body: Naming a review task and responsibility makes coordination clearer. It does not show that the task happened or that the guidance works for every person. Keep later evidence of use and effect distinct rather than claim success from a well-written sentence.

items.title: Use the questions flexibly
items.body: The four questions invite specificity without prescribing a template, quota or measure for every deliverable. A separate equity plan can be useful when connected to actual responsibilities. The question is whether people can use the arrangement, not whether it follows this course’s preferred document shape.

tabs.label: Only the statement
tabs.body: A commitment can guide choices but may leave the next action unclear in Dana’s project. Ask what practice would help without claiming the statement itself caused a barrier. Keep its purpose while identifying a proposal suited to the actual concern.

tabs.label: Only a required row
tabs.body: Adding rows mechanically can create work unrelated to an identified question and hide a useful process elsewhere. The course does not require one for every deliverable. Clarify the relevant practice and how it connects to the team’s actual planning arrangement.

tabs.label: Purpose with a specific proposal
tabs.body: Dana keeps the usability purpose and proposes a proportionate review with clear responsibility and limits. That supports preparation without approving a release or guaranteeing an effect. A separate plan, existing procedure or integrated row can serve when coordination is clear.

check.question: Which account is most accurate?
check.correct: Dana’s proposed review makes a commitment more actionable; implementation and its effects still need appropriate evidence and processes.
wrong: A clear row proves all guidance is usable.
A commitment without all four drafting answers is not equity work.
Every separate equity plan necessarily fails.
check.feedbackCorrect: The account values purpose and clearer preparation while retaining evidence and process limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A row cannot prove usability. The drafting aid does not define all equity work. A separate plan may support coordination when responsibilities connect. Examine the proposed practice and what remains to be established rather than make a universal document rule.

items.text: The team wants guidance people can use.
The team values relevant perspectives in a decision.
Dana proposes a suitable sample review before release.
The policy lead would coordinate the review within assigned responsibility.
A written line proves universal access.
Only one document format can contain equity work.

lessons.transfer: Use Dana’s an example or privately consider a value you want a practice to express. No actual document, personal account or work result is required.

move.control: You can clarify a proposal without inflating its result.
move.failure: A drafting aid becomes a universal definition or proof of equity.
move.next: Name the purpose, proposed task and what has not yet been established.

intro.heading: Examine a process before reusing its documents
intro.body:
Reusing a document can save time and preserve a sound process. It can also carry an assumption that no longer fits. These are possibilities to examine, not claims that DSD normally copies plans without review or drops equity during a rushed meeting. Ask what the document is for now and which relevant process or evidence already exists.

In the example, Dana sees an earlier guidance-plan description and asks whether its review still fits the current material and users. A missing access row does not establish that the next bulletin will be inaccessible or English-only. An existing communications process may cover those needs. Find it, identify any real gap and avoid duplicating or bypassing the responsible work.

A separate practice vacancy raises a hiring question. Alex finds an older posting with a general analytical requirement and a degree. The current duties include policy writing and partner communication. MMB’s June 2019 qualification guidance connects requirements to duties and advises thoughtful use of minimum and preferred qualifications. Alex can prepare the actual duty account and ask HR how the applicable classification, credential and selection requirements should be reviewed. The old wording is not automatically wrong, and the course does not authorize Alex to remove it.

Time and staffing pressures are real considerations in the example. Compare authorized options with the appropriate roles; do not assume a leader can create an interim assignment or waive a credential to avoid delay. A welcoming statement can remain, but it does not settle a qualification’s job-related rationale. For learning, use these invented questions rather than submit an actual selection file.

items.title: Reuse with a purpose check
items.body: Dana can ask which user and material changes affect the review. If an existing process is adequate, the draft can refer to it rather than invent another quota. If a concern remains, make it specific instead of calling the whole template inequitable without evidence.

items.title: Review both kinds of qualification
items.body: Minimum and preferred requirements each communicate what the selection values. Moving a degree to preferred does not settle its relationship to duties. Ask HR about the actual role, consistent assessment and applicable requirements before presenting a proposed change as authorized.

items.title: Handle interim questions separately
items.body: A vacancy can create service and workload pressure. That does not give Alex new staffing or classification authority. Identify the need and seek a workable option through the actual assigned process; retain the difference between requesting help, receiving approval and carrying out an assignment.

tabs.label: Reuse without checking
tabs.body: Old wording can fit, but assuming it does leaves the present duties and concern unexplored. This may preserve a questionable requirement or duplicate a review already handled elsewhere. Ask a current-purpose question instead of equating reuse with either automatic safety or automatic harm.

tabs.label: Change independently
tabs.body: Removing a credential or creating an assignment solely because it seems equitable bypasses the authority question. It can also miss a legitimate requirement. Prepare the rationale and use the actual hiring or staffing process rather than treat an equity intention as permission.

tabs.label: Investigate and coordinate
tabs.body: Alex provides a duty account, asks HR about job-related criteria and raises interim needs with the responsible roles. Dana checks the actual guidance process. These steps examine possible concerns without a guaranteed selection outcome, an invented process fact or a blanket ban on reuse.

check.question: What should Alex do with the older posting?
check.correct: Clarify current duties and review the minimum and preferred requirements with HR through the applicable process, keeping any interim staffing decision separate.
wrong: Remove the degree immediately because every degree excludes unfairly.
Repost unchanged because an older file is always correct.
Add a welcoming statement and declare the qualification concern resolved.
check.feedbackCorrect: This investigates the current role and retains the actual authority and selection questions.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A degree is not automatically inappropriate for every role. Age of a file cannot establish that it still fits. A welcoming statement does not resolve a criterion’s rationale. Review actual duties and requirements rather than assume the conclusion or authorize a change yourself.

items.text: Which duties does the role actually perform now?
Does an existing process address the guidance concern?
Ask HR about required and preferred criteria under the actual classification.
Raise an interim staffing need through its responsible process.
An old file proves all criteria are wrong.
An equity intention authorizes removing any credential.

Declare the old file correct because it was once used.

This investigates and coordinates without assuming the decision.
Past use does not establish current fit.

move.control: You can raise a specific concern and prepare its rationale.
move.failure: Reuse is treated as proof of harm, or a concern is mistaken for authority to change.

lessons.title: Choose evidence that fits the question
lessons.summary: Distinguish activity, usability and outcome evidence in Dana’s project.

Explain why missing evidence leaves causal and effect claims unresolved.
takeaways: Useful evidence depends on the decision and people affected.
A group breakdown is not required or suitable for every practice.
An average, a difference or silence cannot settle every effect or cause.
lessons.statement: Use appropriate evidence and retain what it cannot show.

image.caption: Colleagues examine plans and decisions together.

intro.heading: Choose evidence that fits the question
intro.body:
Evidence should answer the actual question. In Dana’s guidance project, a release log might show that a file was published, a suitable review might identify usability questions and later permitted information might help examine use. These are different claims. Attendance at a consultation or completion of training can be useful activity information without proving that a product improved.

Differences across groups can be important when the question and data support examining them. The DHS Equity Policy’s analysis requirements remain applicable, but this course does not create a universal duty to break every indicator down by group. Consider whether the information is authorized to be collected, used and shared; whether groups and denominators are comparable; whether observations are reliable; and whether people could be identified or harmed by disclosure. Sufficient counts alone do not settle privacy or authority.

In a practice small-region report, Dana’s team lacks permission and sufficiently reliable detail for a proposed breakdown. Publishing the cells with a caveat would not resolve those concerns. Consult the responsible data-practices and analytical roles, consider a suitable permitted alternative and state what remains unknown. A broader figure may answer a limited question without exposing the detail; it also cannot describe every subgroup.

A missing complaint or unavailable figure must not be interpreted as reassuring evidence that access is equitable. A difference, when responsibly observed, does not alone establish its cause. You can compare these sample evidence choices or privately reflect on what you tend to count as convincing. No personal record, demographic information or operational metric is required for this learning.

items.title: Different evidence, different claim
items.body: A release log can show an action while a usability observation concerns a task performed with the material. Neither automatically establishes a service outcome for everyone. Name the claim before selecting an indicator so an easy count does not become a proxy for the entire purpose.

items.title: Permission and privacy come first
items.body: A readable small-group table can still expose people or use information outside its authorized purpose. A note about low counts does not repair that. Identify the actual permitted use and safe reporting approach with responsible staff before analysis or sharing.

items.title: Keep uncertainty informative
items.body: If the team cannot examine a particular difference, say that the question remains open. A permitted alternative can offer limited information without claiming completeness. Do not invent success, a causal story or a failure from missing evidence; name the next appropriate inquiry.

tabs.label: Require a breakdown everywhere
tabs.body: This makes a measure fit the routine rather than the purpose and may invite inappropriate collection or disclosure. Some questions need another kind of evidence. Examine group differences where relevant and supported while preserving authorized use, privacy and interpretation limits.

tabs.label: Publish small cells with a caveat
tabs.body: A limitation note helps readers interpret evidence but cannot authorize data use or prevent identification by itself. Consider the actual risks and permitted alternatives before sharing. Do not treat having a denominator or enough counts as complete clearance.

tabs.label: Match evidence and limits
tabs.body: Dana can use suitable authorized observations, document their scope and seek proper advice about unresolved data questions. Activity and effect remain distinct. This permits meaningful review without a universal measure, a guarantee of improvement or reassurance from silence.

check.question: What should happen when a proposed small-region breakdown lacks appropriate permission and privacy safeguards?
check.correct: Do not publish it merely with a caveat; consult responsible roles, consider a suitable permitted alternative and keep the unanswered question open.
wrong: Publish whenever the count is above an invented course threshold.
Declare there are no disparities because the breakdown is unavailable.
Require every employee to provide new demographic information for the course.
check.feedbackCorrect: The answer retains authority, privacy and honest uncertainty before a measure is used or shared.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The course supplies no clearance threshold. Unavailable information does not prove equity. Learners should not collect personal demographic data for practice. Choose evidence through its actual purpose and permitted use, with reliability and privacy questions addressed.

items.text: A release log records when a file was published.
A suitable permitted observation identifies a usability difficulty.
Is the proposed data use and disclosure authorized?
Are the comparison and privacy safeguards appropriate?
Missing subgroup data proves there are no differences.
A caveat automatically makes any small-cell publication safe.

responses: A caveat cannot establish authorization or privacy.
A publication action does not prove universal use.

lessons.transfer: Use the example to match a claim to evidence and identify one limit. Or privately examine how your own certainty changes when information is missing; no data collection is required.

move.control: You can keep an evidence claim proportionate and honest.
move.failure: A measure becomes compulsory or missing information becomes reassurance.
move.next: Name the question, permitted evidence and what remains unestablished.

lessons.title: Write a useful proposal in the document that serves it

Partners can contribute without becoming automatic task owners.
A draft supports the applicable process; it does not approve itself.
lessons.statement: Make the proposal usable without changing who can decide.

intro.heading: Write a useful proposal in the document that serves it
intro.body:
The four questions can help express a proposal plainly. In Dana’s fiction: examine a guidance sample for identified usability questions; the policy lead coordinates within assigned responsibility; record relevant permitted observations and proposed revisions; review at a suitable point before the planned release. The number of participants, their contribution and the actual review process depend on the task. This is not an official form or a required quota.

The proposal could sit in a work plan, a linked equity plan or an established procedure. Choose the arrangement that keeps responsibilities and the decision visible. An outside partner can offer a perspective or review material without owning the team’s production or approval. Do not transfer delivery to the consultant or a community group merely to make the line look accountable.

For a posting, a useful draft describes actual duties and raises qualification questions for the applicable HR and classification review. MMB guidance connects criteria to responsibilities, with both minimum and preferred qualifications considered thoughtfully. Equivalent experience may be relevant under the applicable process, but the course does not grant a universal degree waiver or tell a panel to change requirements after applications arrive.

For priorities, identify why the work matters, the real constraints and a suitable review point. Ongoing work can be described as ongoing with useful checks. A release deadline does not authorize omitting a required analysis, bypassing a formal review or promising accessible material that has not been examined. You can prepare these practice lines privately rather than change a live document or promise a partner’s participation.

lessons.keyStatement: Make the proposal usable without changing who can decide.

items.title: A worked planning line
items.body: Dana’s line names a review question and coordination role rather than promising all needs will be met. Its evidence concerns what the review found and changed. Later use remains another question. This specificity helps people discuss the proposal without mistaking it for a verified product outcome.

items.title: Roles must be agreed, not invented
items.body: A partner might review a sample or advise on a concern. That contribution needs appropriate invitation and agreement; it does not automatically make the partner accountable for release. The assigned staff role retains delivery, and the actual decision role retains its authority.

items.title: A posting draft is preparation
items.body: Alex can identify policy-writing duties and ask how they should be assessed consistently. HR can advise on the actual qualification and classification process. Keep that inquiry distinct from a unilateral removal, a preferred-criterion shortcut or a claim that a changed pool guarantees a better hire.

tabs.label: One required document shape
tabs.body: Insisting on a row in every deliverable may duplicate a sound procedure and obscure a linked plan. Assess whether the arrangement is understandable and used, not whether it reproduces the course. Keep the proposal, roles and applicable decisions connected across the actual documents.

tabs.label: An external owner for appearance
tabs.body: Naming a partner as owner without agreement or authority can create false accountability and transfer staff work to others. A partner can offer an important perspective while the team still produces and follows through. State the actual contribution rather than satisfy a practice method requirement.

tabs.label: A clear proposed practice
tabs.body: Dana’s line connects an identified question, staff responsibility, suitable evidence and a review opportunity. The arrangement can be integrated or linked. It remains a proposal subject to the applicable processes, without guaranteeing participation, access or a selection result.

check.question: Which revision is a useful proposal rather than a guarantee or transfer of authority?
check.correct: Propose a suitable sample review of the guidance, with the assigned staff role coordinating, agreed partner contributions, permitted observations and an appropriate review point.
wrong: Name an unconsulted community group as owner of the release.
Promise every format and language will be usable because the plan says so.
Remove a required credential from the posting before the applicable review.
check.feedbackCorrect: The proposal clarifies the work and actual roles while retaining evidence and authorization questions.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An unconsulted partner is not an automatic owner. A written promise cannot verify usability. A posting proposal does not authorize changing credentials. Make the task and contributions clear while keeping actual delivery, evidence and decisions in their proper roles.

items.text: Name the usability question the sample review would examine.
Identify permitted observations and an appropriate review point.
The assigned staff role retains production responsibility.
The actual hiring process reviews the proposed qualification change.
A partner named without agreement becomes owner of all delivery.
A row guarantees every language and format need is met.

lessons.title: Use the appropriate process for an actual request or decision
lessons.summary: Distinguish a planning proposal from an accommodation request or workplace concern.
lessons.objective: Distinguish a planning proposal from an accommodation request or workplace concern.

Identify an authority question without inventing the agency’s delegation.

Manager medical-documentation requests and required reporting have specific boundaries.
Equity purpose does not supply all staffing, grant or hiring authority.
lessons.statement: Keep the proposal visible and respond through the responsibility that actually applies.

intro.heading: Use the appropriate process for an actual request or decision
intro.body:
A planning routine must not absorb a person’s actual request. If an employee asks for a schedule change because of a medical condition, that can be an accommodation request even without special terminology. Under MMB Policy 1433, a supervisor should promptly forward the request to the appropriate decision maker and identify that person to the employee. Agency delegation determines who can decide; the policy’s examples do not establish DHS’s actual delegation. A general scheduling proposal can remain separate.

Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation. Where an appropriate documentation request is needed, that responsibility belongs to the agency ADA Coordinator. The policy prohibits requesting or accepting medical records. Do not create a private medical file for a course activity or ask coworkers to vote on a diagnosis. Actual accommodation information follows its proper confidential process.

A harassment or discrimination allegation also retains its actual procedure. Under MMB Policy 1436, supervisors and managers must immediately report allegations and incidents to HR or an Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. A planning discussion or consultant meeting is not a reason to wait. Assigned investigation and response roles remain with the authorized agency process; the course makes no finding about a complaint.

A proposal about grant scoring, payment, qualifications or interim staffing needs its applicable authority and review before a change is represented as approved. Staff can develop the rationale and use consultant guidance without transferring all work to the consultant. Where the role is uncertain, identify the actual question and appropriate contact rather than invent a universal contact or promise. Use these practice situations instead of actual medical, complaint or selection records.

items.title: Recognize and forward the request
items.body: A plain request tied to a medical condition should not wait for the team plan to be adopted. Promptly use the appropriate accommodation decision process and identify the decision maker. A permitted delegated decision is possible under actual agency rules; do not replace that question with a blanket course ban or invented supervisor authority.

items.title: Keep medical documentation with the proper role
items.body: A supervisor’s curiosity about a diagnosis does not authorize requesting information. The ADA Coordinator handles appropriate documentation responsibilities, and the policy prohibits medical-record requests or acceptance. This is a concrete boundary, not merely a warning against collecting too much history.

items.title: Report through the actual process
items.body: A manager hearing a Policy 1436 allegation must immediately report to HR or an Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. The consultant can guide learning but does not replace this duty. Actual assigned investigation roles are preserved rather than improvised or universally prohibited by the course.

tabs.label: Solve the request with a plan line
tabs.body: A general flexible-scheduling proposal cannot replace the individual accommodation process. Waiting for the plan can delay the actual request, while collecting medical information privately breaches the manager boundary. Keep the broad proposal and the prompt response separate.

tabs.label: Approve every equity proposal
tabs.body: A sound purpose does not establish payment, staffing, qualification or grant authority. Present the rationale as a recommendation and identify the required review. The proposal can remain worth pursuing while some actual decisions stay with another role or process.

tabs.label: Prepare and use the proper roles
tabs.body: The team continues its work while the actual accommodation, reporting or decision question follows its procedure. This avoids both abandoning the concern and claiming unsupported authority. It retains staff ownership, useful consultant feedback and the difference between advice, decision and implementation.

check.question: A supervisor hears a schedule-change request tied to a medical condition. What should happen?
check.correct: Promptly forward it to the appropriate accommodation decision maker and identify that person; do not request medical information, and keep any general plan proposal separate.
wrong: Wait for the planning document before considering the request.
Request the employee’s medical records for a private manager file.
Approve any requested change solely because this course favors equity.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response recognizes the request, retains actual delegation and respects the manager medical-information boundary.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The request should not wait for a general plan. Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or records for private files. The course supplies no blanket decision authority. Use the actual prompt accommodation process and its proper roles.

Promptly forward an accommodation request and identify its appropriate decision maker.

Wait for consultation before required reporting.
A supervisor requests medical records to settle a planning question.

intro.heading: Review the gain and choose a next inquiry
intro.body:
Dana’s original commitment said the guidance should be more usable. The revised practice proposal names a suitable review question, a staff coordination role, possible agreed contributions, permitted evidence and a review opportunity. Comparing the two shows clearer preparation. It does not show that partners accepted an invitation, a decision was made or users experienced an improvement.

A review can identify what remains: an evidence option may need authorization, an accessibility question may need responsible expertise or a proposed qualification may need the actual HR process. Make the next question and role clear. An unresolved issue is not automatically a failure of staff or a reason to invent an external owner. A deadline should fit the actual work and authority rather than a universal course instruction to edit by Friday.

If an appropriate change is later authorized and carried out, its use and contribution can be examined with suitable evidence. A document pair supports the account of preparation. An activity log supports an action claim. A meaningful effect needs its own basis and limits. Missing evidence remains unknown, and a quiet complaint record does not establish that all barriers disappeared.

Personal reflection can be equally worthwhile. You might recognize that a polished plan had felt like the whole result, or that written detail was being valued above relationships and understanding. That insight can remain private and need not produce an operational artifact. Use Dana’s fiction, another invented draft or an unrecorded personal question. Consultant feedback and partner perspectives can help while staff retain their work and actual decisions remain with responsible roles.

inThisLesson: Compare an original and revised practice proposal without claiming implementation.
Identify a remaining evidence or authority question and a proportionate next step.
Recognize learning through private reflection as well as work application.
Which conclusion should be used?
lessons.keyStatement: Keep the specific gain, the remaining question and the next step that fits.

items.title: Compare what actually changed
items.body: Dana’s revision clarifies a proposed task and responsibility rather than adding a success claim. That is a useful gain. Identify the difference specifically so a clearer sentence is not mistaken for approved participation, implemented access or a proven service effect.

items.title: A next step can address a real limit
items.body: If data cannot be used appropriately, the next step may be asking the responsible role about a suitable alternative. It need not be mandatory disaggregation or publication with a caveat. The purpose is to make the question actionable without granting new authority or promising an answer.

items.title: Keep the personal path valid
items.body: Privately reconsidering what commitment and responsibility mean can deepen understanding even without editing a work file. A practice path permits the same reasoning without disclosure. Work application may follow, but it is not a performance test for the value of the learning.

tabs.label: Call the draft the outcome
tabs.body: This inflates a preparation gain and hides the remaining decision and evidence work. The draft may be valuable, but its claim should remain clear. Keep later approval, action and effect separate rather than use the plan’s polish as proof of equity.

tabs.label: Require a live edit and a metric
tabs.body: This can pressure learners to alter material outside their role or disclose work information. A private or practice path is legitimate. Any actual change needs its appropriate authority and evidence, while personal understanding is worthwhile without a work product.

tabs.label: Review with honest limits
tabs.body: Dana can identify the improved proposal, unresolved question and appropriate next role. A learner can privately retain an insight or choose another practice. This keeps ownership and agency without a prescribed deadline, compulsory external owner or invented success claim.

check.question: Which closing account is accurate?
check.correct: The revised practice proposal is clearer; implementation and effects remain unestablished, and further private learning or appropriate work inquiry can be chosen.
wrong: A document pair proves all affected groups benefited.
A missing breakdown establishes that no disparity exists.
Every learner must change a live posting by Friday to count as learning.
check.feedbackCorrect: The answer preserves the specific preparation gain and values both learning paths with honest limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A document pair cannot prove benefits for all groups. Missing information does not establish absence of disparity. The course does not require a live edit or deadline. Keep the learning gain, actual evidence limits and chosen next inquiry distinct.

items.text: Dana’s proposal now makes coordination clearer.
A learner privately recognizes an assumption about what a plan proves.
Which appropriate role can advise on the evidence option?
Choose another practice comparison or private inquiry.
Every affected person benefited because the plan changed.
A compulsory live edit is the only legitimate learning outcome.

scenario.context: DSD practice case: Dana’s proposal improves, but partner agreement, authorization and actual effects remain unestablished.
options: Keep the preparation gain and the unresolved questions, with appropriate next roles and private learning.
Declare all effects verified from the revised plan.
Make an outside partner the automatic owner so the method passes.
responses: This retains clear evidence, staff ownership and agency.
A draft cannot establish those effects.
The course does not invent agreement or responsibility.

lessons.transfer: Privately retain a question about commitment and practice, or compare Dana’s practice drafts. No live edit, entered notes, partner contact or measured effect is required.

move.control: You can name a learning gain and an appropriate next question.
move.failure: A useful proposal becomes proof of results or a compulsory work assignment.
move.next: Keep the preparation, actual decision, action and effect distinct as inquiry continues.

jobAid.subtitle: Clarify a proposed practice without overstating its authority or effects.
remember: Task, responsibility, evidence and review point are optional drafting questions, not a definition of all equity work or the formal DHS analysis.
Staff retain delivery; partners and the consultant can contribute guidance without becoming automatic owners.
Private or practice learning is legitimate without entered notes, an actual edit or a measured work result.

sections.heading: Understand the current work
items: Identify the commitment and the specific barrier or question.
Find existing processes before assuming a missing row means missing practice.
Use the document arrangement that supports coordination, including a linked plan where useful.

sections.heading: Prepare the proposal
items: Describe the task and the role responsible within actual authority.
Agree relevant partner contributions rather than assign ownership on paper.
Choose evidence suited to the question and permitted use, with privacy, reliability and comparability checked.
Choose a meaningful review point; ongoing work can have recurring checks.

sections.heading: Retain actual responsibilities
items: Use the applicable DHS analysis process for an actual action.
Review hiring criteria, classification and interim staffing through their authorized processes.
Promptly forward accommodation requests and identify the appropriate decision maker; managers must not request medical information or documentation.
Retain ADA Coordinator documentation responsibilities and the prohibition on requesting or accepting medical records.
Supervisors and managers immediately report Policy 1436 allegations and incidents to HR or an Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures.

sections.heading: Review and continue
items: Distinguish a revised draft, actual decision, implementation and effect.
Keep missing information open rather than reassuring or inventing a cause.
Identify a proportionate next question and proper role without a course-imposed deadline.
Choose private reflection, practice or appropriate work application with useful guidance.
